Actually wait — this is really important. pnpm install is failing because of the minimumReleaseAge check. The error was this:
```
[ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION] 7 lockfile entries failed verification:
  @firebase/auth-types@0.13.2 could not be checked against minimumReleaseAge (The operation was aborted due to timeout)
```

"could not be checked against minimumReleaseAge (The operation was aborted due to timeout)" — this is because the network is extremely slow, and pnpm couldn't fetch the metadata (the "time" field) to verify the release age, so the check timed out. In other words, the root cause is the slow network + the minimumReleaseAge policy.

But where does minimumReleaseAge come from? Let me check. It might be a pnpm 11 default. Let me look at the code around line 64856, `minimumReleaseAge = opts2.minimumReleaseAge ?? 0` — the default is 0 (disabled). So it must be set somewhere.

Let me search more thoroughly. Actually, let me check the pnpm-workspace.yaml in app again, and also check the possibility that pnpm 11 is reading from somewhere. Let me directly check what value pnpm resolves.
